title: Transcriptomic and Regulatory Network Responses to Heat and Dim Light During Tomato Seed Maturation
content: Late seed maturation determines seed vigor and stress resilience, yet the transcriptional networks connecting environmental stress to seed quality remain poorly characterized. To investigate the effect of temperature and light on molecular processes that may lead to altered seed vigor, we use a tissue-specific seed transcriptome (i.e., embryo and endosperm) dataset and physiologic response of tomato (Solanum lycopersicum cv. Moneymaker) dissected from fruits that were ripened ex planta under four different environmental conditions (i.e., standard or high temperature and/or standard or dim light). First, to dissect the transcriptional responses underlying seed vigor, we used weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). This revealed a distinct tissue-specific expression program. In both tissues, Heat dominated the molecular response by 10 significant associations from 14 total associations, followed by dim light (3 associations) and 1 association for combined stress. Germination rate declined as stress-responsive transcriptional activity intensified. Furthermore, the combined heat and dim-light treatment elicited non-additive transcriptional responses, indicating that temperature and light can act through opposing regulatory programs during seed maturation. Next, to uncover the candidate regulators of heat and/or dim light responsive modules, we use a random forest network inference approach (GENIE3). Network inference predicted 13 major candidate hub transcription factors (TFs), dominated by ethylene-responsive (ERF), C2H2 zinc finger, GRAS, and B3-domain transcription factors, of which several (PRE4, TRF, NAC, Dof, bZIP) represent novel candidates for functionally validation in light response during seed maturation studies. Together, these findings demonstrate that temperature and light conditions during postharvest tomato fruit maturation are associated with distinct tissue-specific transcriptional networks and differences in seed germination performance, providing a set of candidate regulatory genes for future functional characterization.
